config.title: CDN & edge computing

intro.title: CDN & edge computing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a conceptual model of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to understand how it accelerates web content delivery. You'll learn the core concept of edge computing, which brings computation and data storage closer to users to reduce latency. The main technologies involved are CDN servers, origin servers, and caching strategies. You'll explore how static assets like images and videos are distributed globally. By the end, you'll grasp how CDNs improve performance and reliability for modern web applications.
intro.usecase: CDNs and edge computing are foundational to modern web performance and user experience. They power the fast loading of images, videos, and scripts on content-heavy sites like news portals and e-commerce platforms (e.g., product galleries on Amazon). Developers use them to deploy serverless functions globally, enabling features like real-time form validation, personalized dashboard content, and low-latency API calls for interactive applications. This pattern is critical for building scalable, responsive systems that serve a global user base without performance degradation.

objectives: Configure a CDN to cache and serve static assets from edge locations
Implement edge computing logic to process user requests closer to their origin
Construct a content delivery strategy that minimizes latency for global users
Apply cache-control headers to manage asset freshness and reduce origin server load
Integrate edge functions to execute custom logic at distributed network locations
Manipulate request routing to direct traffic through optimal edge paths
Initialize a simulated edge environment to test proximity-based content delivery
